sample_unit: questions (each asked under 4 prompt forms to 2 chatbots)

links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of chatbot hypertension responses versus NIH recommendations
links.effect: Most responses were at collegiate reading level, above NIH recommendations; ChatGPT had a higher FK grade level than Gemini across all forms.
links.quote: The grade level for most responses was collegiate level, which was above average for the National Institutes of Health (NIH) recommendations, but on par with most online medical information.

links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education responses on hypertension
links.effect: Responses were mostly collegiate reading level, above NIH recommendations; ChatGPT had higher FK grade than Gemini across all forms.
links.quote: The grade level for most responses was collegiate level, which was above average for the National Institutes of Health (NIH) recommendations, but on par with most online medical information.

unlisted_practices: Patient-friendly prompting to alter response style, compared with no prompting, physician-level prompting and prompting for statistics/references

screen.practice: reading-level and audience prompting (patient-friendly vs physician-level prompts)
screen.reason: The study empirically tests how different prompting strategies (such as patient-friendly prompting vs standard or physician-level prompting) affect readability and correctness of LLM outputs for patient education.
